nodes.notes:
ANALYSIS:
1) Classification: Conv2d 3x3 (in=64, out=128, stride=1, pad=1) fp16 + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2) on input [1,64,360,640]. quantize=False so QConv2D acts as plain Conv2d, activation_quantizer is identity (quantize_act=False). Output [1,128,180,320].
2) Canonical: y[oc,oh,ow]=relu(sum_ic,kh,kw x[ic,oh+kh-1,ow+kw-1]*W[oc,ic,kh,kw]+b[oc]); pooled[oc,ph,pw]=mean(y[oc,2ph:2ph+2,2pw:2pw+2]).
3) Layout: NCHW fp16 contiguous. Weights [128,64,3,3] fp16. Reduction over (ic,kh,kw)=576. Pool reduces 4x output writes.
4) Regimes: (a) Memory-bound conv at this resolution; (b) compute-bound if larger channels; (c) launch/overhead-bound at small spatial sizes.
5) Knobs: cudnn vs custom Triton implicit gemm; fuse relu+pool; tile (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_H, BLOCK_W); use TF32/FP16 tensor cores via tl.dot.
6) Skeleton: each program computes a tile of pooled output (2x2 of conv outputs per pooled element) for a block of OC; load weights once, sweep IC; accumulate fp32; relu; pool 2x2 average; store.
7) Families: F1 cuDNN-backed (call torch.nn.functional.conv2d then fused triton relu+avgpool); F2 fully-fused triton implicit-GEMM conv+relu+avgpool; F3 torch.compile-style channels_last + fused tail.
SELF_CHECK: families differ in kernel boundary; only one chosen per plan.

action.description: Use torch.nn.functional.conv2d (cuDNN fp16) for the conv, then a single fused Triton kernel that performs ReLU + AvgPool2d(2) on the conv output, writing the pooled result directly. Bypass QConv2D quantization since quantize=False.
action.rationale: cuDNN conv on fp16 is highly optimized for RTX5090 tensor cores; the bottleneck removed is the python overhead of QConv2D plus separate relu/pool kernels. Fusing relu+avgpool reduces memory traffic ~2x for the tail.
action.title: cuDNN conv + fused Triton ReLU+AvgPool tail

kernel_summary: Forward pass of a ConvBlock: fp16 Conv2d 3x3 (in=64, out=128, stride=1, pad=1, bias=True) on input [1,64,360,640], followed by ReLU, an identity activation_quantizer (quantize=False), and AvgPool2d(2) producing [1,128,180,320]. Since quantize_conv/quantize_act are False, QConv2D reduces to standard Conv2d. The kernel is a mix of compute-heavy 3x3 conv (well-served by cuDNN/tensor cores) and a memory-bound tail (relu+avgpool). Key constraints: fp16 dtype throughout, NCHW input by default, must match numerics within fp16 tolerance, weights/bias must be reused from the original module. Main optimization levers: bypass quantization Python overhead, pick best cuDNN algo (channels_last), and fuse ReLU+AvgPool into a single Triton kernel to halve tail memory traffic.
open_questions: Does torch.compile baseline already pick channels_last + fused tail, limiting headroom?
What is the baseline split between conv time and relu+avgpool time at this resolution?
Does cuDNN on RTX5090 prefer NHWC fp16 strongly enough to overcome layout conversion cost?
Are weights stored fp16 in the existing QConv2D and directly usable, or does QConv2D apply any nontrivial transform when quantize=False?
Is the activation_quantizer truly identity when quantize_act=False (does create_quantizer return None or a passthrough)?
What tolerance does the evaluator use for fp16 correctness comparison?
Is the input always batch=1 and exactly 360x640, or can shapes vary at eval time?
